question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rewrite:
Task: For each customer and for every calendar month in the requested reporting period, compute the customer's account closing balance at the end of that month, the month-over-month change (difference between this month's closing balance and the previous month's closing balance for the same customer), and the running cumulative bank account balance across months for that customer; include months with no transactions by carrying forward the prior balance so that every month in the period appears for every customer.
Required outputs: customer identifier (unique key that identifies the customer); year (integer, calendar year of the month); month (integer 1-12, calendar month); month_end_date (date representing the last calendar date of the month); closing_balance (numeric: customer's account balance as of the month_end_date; if no transactions in or before the month, treat as zero or initial balance as per data); month_over_month_change (numeric: closing_balance for this month minus closing_balance for prior month for same customer; for the first month in the reporting period for a customer, compute change relative to the prior month's balance which may be zero or prior-data balance if available); cumulative_balance (numeric: running cumulative sum of closing_balance values across months for the customer in chronological order within the reporting period)
Filters: Include every customer present in the customer dataset (or in transaction dataset) — each customer must have one row per calendar month in the reporting period, even if they have no transactions that month; Reporting period: every calendar month between the specified start_date and end_date inclusive (these input literal dates must be provided when executing the query); rows must be generated for each month in that inclusive range; Balance carry-forward rule: if a customer has no transactions in a month, the closing_balance for that month equals the previous month's closing_balance for that customer (or an initial balance of zero if no prior balance exists); Treat transaction effects and opening balances according to the source data when computing closing balances; do not drop customers or months for lack of activity
Sort/limit: Order the output by customer identifier ascending, then by year ascending, then by month ascending; no row limit unless an external limit is specified

required_filters.note: Start and end dates of the reporting period must be supplied at query time; the relation is restricted to months between those dates inclusive.

subgoals.text: Generate one row per calendar month in the inclusive reporting period. Each row represents a single month with its year, month number, and month_end_date. This produces the master set of months to cross-join with customers so that every month appears.

required_filters.note: May optionally include all customers appearing in transactions by union; do not filter out inactive customers.

subgoals.text: Canonical list of every customer to include. One row per customer with the customer identifier and any canonical opening/initial balance if available in customer master data. This cohort covers all customers present in customer data or transaction data.

required_filters.note: Includes every customer x month in the reporting period; months are filled even with no transactions by carrying forward balances.

subgoals.text: For each customer x month (every combination from customers_cohort cross-joined with report_months_calendar), compute the closing_balance as of the month_end_date by applying all transactions and any initial/opening balances up to that date. Also compute month_over_month_change (closing_balance minus prior month's closing_balance for same customer) and cumulative_balance (running sum of closing_balance across months per customer in chronological order). Carry forward prior balance for months with no transactions per customer (i.e., closing_balance repeats previous month's closing_balance or uses initial_balance/zero if no prior).

final_sql:
WITH customers_cohort AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  NULL AS initial_balance
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id FROM customer_nodes
  UNION
  SELECT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
)
),
customer_monthly_closing_balances AS (
SELECT
  cc.customer_id AS customer_id,
  strftime('%Y', rm.month_start) AS year,
  strftime('%m', rm.month_start) AS month,
  rm.month_end AS month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance: sum of initial_balance + all txn_amounts up to month_end_date
  COALESCE(
    cc.initial_balance,
    0
  )
  +
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(ct.txn_amount)
    FROM customer_transactions ct
    WHERE ct.customer_id = cc.customer_id
      AND date(ct.txn_date) <= date(rm.month_end)
  ), 0) AS closing_balance,
  -- month_over_month_change: closing_balance minus prior month's closing_balance
  (
    (
      COALESCE(cc.initial_balance,0)
      +
      COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(ct2.txn_amount)
        FROM customer_transactions ct2
        WHERE ct2.customer_id = cc.customer_id
          AND date(ct2.txn_date) <= date(rm.month_end)
      ),0)
    )
    -
    (
      COALESCE(cc.initial_balance,0)
      +
      COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(ct3.txn_amount)
        FROM customer_transactions ct3
        WHERE ct3.customer_id = cc.customer_id
          AND date(ct3.txn_date) <= date(date(rm.month_start, '-1 day'))
      ),0)
    )
  ) AS month_over_month_change,
  -- cumulative_balance: running sum of closing_balance across months per customer
  (
    SELECT SUM(
      COALESCE(cc2.initial_balance,0)
      +
      COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(ct4.txn_amount)
        FROM customer_transactions ct4
        WHERE ct4.customer_id = cc.customer_id
          AND date(ct4.txn_date) <= date(rm2.month_end)
      ),0)
    )
    FROM customers_cohort cc2
    JOIN (
      -- generate same report months rows via recursive approach substitution:
      -- but to keep view self-contained, assume there exists same months in customers_cohort join space
      -- replicate rows by selecting distinct month starts/ends from a calendar derived from transactions and node dates
      SELECT DISTINCT
        date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date))) AS month_start,
        date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
      FROM customer_transactions t
      UNION
      SELECT DISTINCT
        date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date))) AS month_start,
        date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
      FROM customer_nodes
    ) rm2 ON 1=1
    WHERE cc2.customer_id = cc.customer_id
      AND (date(rm2.month_end) <= date(rm.month_end))
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM customers_cohort cc
-- derive report months calendar by union of months present in data to ensure every month in reporting period is present
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date))) AS month_start,
    date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(t.txn_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
  FROM customer_transactions t
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date))) AS month_start,
    date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(start_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end
  FROM customer_nodes
) rm ON 1=1
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  m.year,
  m.month,
  m.month_end_date,
  cmb.closing_balance,
  cmb.month_over_month_change,
  cmb.cumulative_balance
FROM customers_cohort AS c
CROSS JOIN (
  -- generate months between start and end dates inclusive
  WITH params AS (
    SELECT date('2020-01-01') AS start_date, date('2020-12-31') AS end_date
  ),
  months AS (
    SELECT
      strftime('%Y', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) AS year,
      CAST(strftime('%m', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) AS INTEGER) AS month,
      date(strftime('%Y', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) || '-' ||
           strftime('%m', date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months')) || '-01', '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date
    FROM params,
         (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
          UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
          UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17
          UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23
          UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
          UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
          UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41
          UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47
          UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53
          UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
          UNION ALL SELECT 60) AS nums
    WHERE date(params.start_date, '+' || (n) || ' months') <= params.end_date
  )
  SELECT year, month, month_end_date FROM months
) AS m
LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_closing_balances AS cmb
  ON cmb.customer_id = c.customer_id
  AND cmb.year = CAST(m.year AS INTEGER)
  AND cmb.month = m.month
ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC, m.year ASC, m.month ASC

question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rewrite:
Task: For each customer and for each calendar month in 2020, compute that customer's month-end balance defined as the sum of deposit amounts minus the sum of withdrawal amounts that occurred during that calendar month; then find (1) the month in 2020 with the largest count of customers whose month-end balance is strictly greater than zero and (2) the month in 2020 with the smallest count of customers whose month-end balance is strictly greater than zero; for each of those two months compute the average of the month-end balances across all customers (including customers with zero or negative month-end balances), and finally report the difference between those two monthly averages (average_for_month_with_highest_positive_count minus average_for_month_with_lowest_positive_count).
Required outputs: month_with_highest_positive_count (calendar month in 2020, e.g., '2020-03' or month number 1-12); highest_positive_customer_count (integer count of distinct customers with month-end balance > 0 in that month); average_month_end_balance_for_highest_month (numeric average of month-end balances across all customers for that month); month_with_lowest_positive_count (calendar month in 2020); lowest_positive_customer_count (integer count of distinct customers with month-end balance > 0 in that month); average_month_end_balance_for_lowest_month (numeric average of month-end balances across all customers for that month); difference_between_averages (numeric: average_for_highest_month minus average_for_lowest_month)
Filters: consider only transactions that occurred on dates within the calendar year 2020 (i.e., transaction date >= '2020-01-01' and <= '2020-12-31'); for month grouping use calendar months January through December 2020 (12 distinct months); month-end balance for a given customer and month = (sum of amounts of all transactions classified as deposits within that month) minus (sum of amounts of all transactions classified as withdrawals within that month); if a customer has no transactions in a month their month-end balance = 0; positive month-end balance means strictly greater than 0 (> 0); average month-end balance for a month is the arithmetic mean of the month-end balances for all customers (include every customer present in the customers dataset or relevant customer list, even if their balance is zero for that month)

subgoals.text: Generate one row per customer for each calendar month in 2020. This produces the complete set of customer-month pairs to ensure customers with no transactions in a month are included (their balances will be computed as zero later).

All transactions in 2020, annotated with customer, calendar month, and a flag/classification for deposit vs withdrawal and transaction amount. This relation is the raw per-transaction data restricted to the 2020 date range and grouped by month later.

For each customer and calendar month in 2020, compute the month-end balance = sum(deposits) - sum(withdrawals). Start from the complete customer-month set and left-join aggregated monthly transactions so customers with no transactions get balance = 0.

final_sql:
WITH all_customers_months_2020 AS (
SELECT
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(months.month_start) AS month_start_date,
  strftime('%Y-%m', months.month_start) || '-01' AS month_label
FROM
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
    FROM customer_nodes
  ) AS c
CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT '2020-01-01' AS month_start UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-02-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-03-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-04-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-05-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-06-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-07-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-08-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-09-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-10-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-11-01' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2020-12-01'
  ) AS months
),
customer_month_transactions_2020 AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS transaction_date,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start_date,
  CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_deposit_flag,
  CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_withdrawal_flag,
  txn_amount AS amount
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date >= '2020-01-01' AND txn_date <= '2020-12-31'
),
customer_month_balances AS (
SELECT
  a.customer_id,
  a.month_start_date,
  a.month_label,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.is_deposit_flag = 1 THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END)
           - SUM(CASE WHEN t.is_withdrawal_flag = 1 THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) AS month_end_balance
FROM all_customers_months_2020 a
LEFT JOIN customer_month_transactions_2020 t
  ON a.customer_id = t.customer_id
  AND a.month_start_date = t.month_start_date
GROUP BY
  a.customer_id,
  a.month_start_date,
  a.month_label
)
SELECT
  high.month_label AS month_with_highest_positive_count,
  high.positive_count AS highest_positive_customer_count,
  high.avg_balance AS average_month_end_balance_for_highest_month,
  low.month_label AS month_with_lowest_positive_count,
  low.positive_count AS lowest_positive_customer_count,
  low.avg_balance AS average_month_end_balance_for_lowest_month,
  (high.avg_balance - low.avg_balance) AS difference_between_averages
FROM
  (
    SELECT month_start_date, month_label,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 END) AS positive_count,
           AVG(month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM customer_month_balances
    WHERE month_start_date >= '2020-01-01' AND month_start_date <= '2020-12-01'
    GROUP BY month_start_date, month_label
    ORDER BY positive_count DESC, month_start_date ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS high
CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT month_start_date, month_label,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 END) AS positive_count,
           AVG(month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM customer_month_balances
    WHERE month_start_date >= '2020-01-01' AND month_start_date <= '2020-12-01'
    GROUP BY month_start_date, month_label
    ORDER BY positive_count ASC, month_start_date ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS low

question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rewrite:
Task: For each customer, aggregate all deposits and withdrawals by month (grouping transactions by the first day of that month) to compute a monthly net amount, compute each customer’s monthly closing balances by cumulatively summing those monthly nets in chronological order, identify each customer's most recent month and its prior month, compute that most recent month’s growth rate as: (most_recent_closing_balance - prior_month_closing_balance) / prior_month_closing_balance, except when prior_month_closing_balance = 0 in which case set growth rate = most_recent_closing_balance * 100, then compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month growth rate is greater than 0.05 (5%).
Required outputs: overall_percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5_percent: numeric value representing the percentage (0-100) of customers whose most recent month growth rate > 0.05; numerator_customers: integer count of customers meeting growth > 5%; denominator_customers: integer count of customers considered (customers having at least two months of balances or one month if prior balance is treated as zero per rule)
Filters: Group transactions into months by mapping each transaction date to the month start date (the first day of that month).; Monthly net amount per customer = sum of deposits and withdrawals in that month, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative.; Monthly closing balance per customer is the cumulative sum of the monthly net amounts ordered by month ascending.; Most recent month per customer = the latest month for which the customer has a monthly net (and thus a closing balance).; Prior month per customer = the immediately preceding month chronologically for that customer; if no prior month exists, treat prior_month_closing_balance = 0 for the growth-rate rule.; Growth-rate comparison threshold = 0.05 (strictly greater than 0.05).

subgoals.text: For each customer and calendar month (map transaction date to month start), sum deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative to produce the monthly net amount.

For each customer, order months chronologically and compute the cumulative sum of monthly_net to produce the closing balance at each month. Also produce a row_number or rank to identify chronology and a lag of the prior month's closing balance.

For each customer select the most recent month (latest month_start). Compute growth_rate = (most_recent_closing_balance - prior_closing_balance) / prior_closing_balance, but if prior_closing_balance = 0 treat growth_rate = most_recent_closing_balance * 100. Output a boolean flag whether growth_rate > 0.05 and include customers with no prior month (treated as prior_closing_balance = 0 per rule).

final_sql:
WITH monthly_nets_per_customer AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
           WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
           ELSE 0 END) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) END AS overall_percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5_percent,
  SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS numerator_customers,
  COUNT(*) AS denominator_customers
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    -- identify most recent month's closing and prior month's closing (prior = 0 if none)
    CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance ELSE NULL END AS most_recent_closing_balance,
    COALESCE(LAG(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 0) AS prior_month_closing_balance,
    -- compute growth_rate per customer (we compute only for rn=1 rows)
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(LAG(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 0) = 0
        THEN CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN closing_balance * 100.0 ELSE NULL END
      ELSE
        CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN (closing_balance - COALESCE(LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 0)) / COALESCE(LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC), 1) ELSE NULL END
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      month_start,
      monthly_net,
      SUM(monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC) AS rn
    FROM monthly_nets_per_customer
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
) s

question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rewrite:
Task: For every month after the first month present in the data, compute the total of all users' balances as of the first day of the previous month, treating any individual negative balances as zero when summing; return one row per month (excluding the first month), where the 'month' identifies the current month and the 'previous_month_total_balance' is the sum computed from balances measured on the 1st day of the previous month.
Required outputs: month — identifier for the current month (use the same month representation as in the schema/data, e.g., a date truncated to month or a year-month string); previous_month_total_balance — numeric total equal to the sum across all users of their balance as of the 1st day of the previous month with each individual negative balance replaced by zero
Filters: Exclude the very first month present in the dataset from the output; use that first month only as the baseline to compute the previous_month_total_balance for the following month; When computing balances for a given previous month, use balances measured specifically on the 1st day of that previous month; Replace any negative per-user balance values with zero before summing them into previous_month_total_balance
Sort/limit: Sort results in ascending order by month; no limit

required_filters.date_is_first_of_month: balance_date is exactly the first day of its month

subgoals.text: Select per-user balance records that fall exactly on the first day of a month. This yields one row per observed balance measurement on a month's first day (do not aggregate).

Build an ordered list of distinct months present in the data, identify the earliest month, and produce one row per month except the very first month. Each row includes the current month and its previous month (previous month = one month earlier).

For each current month from month_list_excluding_first, compute the total across all users of their balance measured on the 1st day of the previous_month, replacing any negative per-user balance with zero before summing. Produce one row per current month with the computed previous_month_total_balance.

inherited_filters.date_is_first_of_month: balance_date is exactly the first day of its month

final_sql:
WITH balances_on_first_of_month AS (
SELECT
  su.user_id AS user_id,
  se.event_time AS balance_date,
  CAST(NULL AS REAL) AS balance
FROM
  shopping_cart_users AS su
JOIN
  shopping_cart_events AS se
  ON su.cookie_id = se.cookie_id
WHERE
  strftime('%d', se.event_time) = '01'
)
SELECT
  strftime('%Y-%m', date(balance_date, '+1 month')) AS month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance END) AS previous_month_total_balance
FROM balances_on_first_of_month
GROUP BY date(balance_date)
HAVING date(balance_date) > (
  SELECT MIN(date(balance_date)) FROM balances_on_first_of_month
)
ORDER BY month ASC

question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rewrite:
Task: Compute, for each calendar month (excluding each customer's first month of transactions), the sum across all customers of that customer's maximum 30-day rolling average daily balance observed within that month, where the daily balance is computed per customer as deposits adding and all other transaction types subtracting, 30-day rolling averages are computed only for days with a full 30-day window and any negative 30-day average is treated as zero.
Required outputs: month: the calendar month (year-month) for which the aggregate is reported; monthly_sum_of_max_30day_avg_balances: numeric total equal to the sum over all customers of each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within that month (after applying the non-negativity rule and excluding customers' first-month data)
Filters: Only include daily balances where deposits add to the balance and all other transaction types subtract.; Compute a 30-day rolling average balance per customer per day only when that customer has 30 days of consecutive historical daily balances available (i.e., a full 30-day window ending on that day); do not produce a rolling-average value for days without a full 30-day history.; If a computed 30-day rolling average for a customer on a day is negative, treat it as zero when considering maxima and sums.; For each customer, identify their first calendar month that contains any transaction(s) and exclude that month entirely from the final aggregated results for that customer.; Group daily 30-day-average values by calendar month (year-month) and for each customer and month take the maximum of that customer's daily 30-day averages within the month (after applying non-negativity).; For each month (across all customers), sum those per-customer monthly maxima to produce the reported monthly total.; Include only months where at least one customer contributes a non-excluded maximum (i.e., months that are not every customer's excluded baseline month).
Sort/limit: order results by month ascending; no row limit

required_filters.txn_sign_rule: deposits are added, all other txn types are subtracted

subgoals.text: Compute each customer's daily balance by date where deposits add and all other transaction types subtract. Produce one row per customer per calendar date that had any transaction activity or a derived balance for that date.

required_filters.full_window: only include dates where the customer has 30 consecutive days of daily_balance ending on that date

subgoals.text: For each customer and date, compute the 30-day rolling average of daily_balance using only days that have a full 30-day historical window ending on that date. If fewer than 30 prior-consecutive days exist for that customer, do not produce a rolling-average row for that date. Apply non-negativity: if the 30-day average is negative, treat it as zero (i.e., output max(average, 0)).

subgoals.text: For each calendar month (year-month), exclude each customer's first calendar month that contains any transaction. For remaining months, for each customer take the maximum rolling_avg_30_nonneg within that month (if any), then sum those per-customer monthly maxima across all customers to produce the monthly total. Output one row per month (year-month) with the aggregated sum. Exclude months that have no contributing customers after exclusions.

final_sql:
WITH customer_daily_balances AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) OVER (
    PARTITION BY customer_id, txn_date
  ) AS daily_balance
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_30day_rolling_avg_nonneg AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.date,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY d.customer_id ORDER BY d.date ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND 0 FOLLOWING) = 30
    THEN MAX( (SUM(daily_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY d.customer_id ORDER BY d.date ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND 0 FOLLOWING)) / 30.0, 0 )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS rolling_avg_30_nonneg
FROM customer_daily_balances d
WHERE 1=1
)

question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rewrite:
Task: For each month, compute the sum across all customers of each customer's maximum daily balance within that month, where each customer's daily balances are defined for every date from their earliest transaction date through their latest transaction date by carrying forward the previous day's balance for days without transactions and treating any negative daily balance as zero.
Required outputs: month (identify month, e.g., YYYY-MM or first-day-of-month date); monthly_total_max_daily_balance (numeric) — sum over customers of that customer's maximum daily balance in the month
Filters: Include only dates between each customer's earliest transaction date and latest transaction date (inclusive).; For days with no transactions for a customer, carry forward that customer's previous day's balance; if there is no prior day within the customer's range, treat the balance as the first available day's balance.; Any daily balance that is negative must be treated as zero before computing monthly maxima and sums.; Consider every customer who has at least one transaction (so an earliest and latest transaction date exist).
Sort/limit: order results chronologically by month ascending; no row limit

subgoals.text: For every customer who has at least one transaction, determine that customer's earliest and latest transaction date and the balance on each transaction date (transactions may have multiple per date; keep per-date net/ending balance).

For each customer, generate one row per calendar date from that customer's first_txn_date through last_txn_date (inclusive). For dates with a transaction, use that date's date_end_balance; for dates without a transaction, carry forward the previous available date's balance. If no previous day within the customer's range exists, use the first_txn_date's balance for earlier days (practically this means the first date is the first_txn_date).

For each customer and calendar month (identify month as e.g., YYYY-MM or first-day-of-month), clip any negative daily_balance to zero, then compute that customer's maximum daily_balance within that month. This relation is one row per customer per month containing the customer's monthly maximum (non-negative) daily balance.

final_sql:
WITH
-- parse txn_date to YYYY-MM-DD
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    txn_amount,
    txn_type
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
-- get customer date ranges
cust_range AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(min(txn_date)) AS start_date,
    date(max(txn_date)) AS end_date
  FROM txns
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- all transaction days per customer with net change (treat deposits positive, withdrawals negative if txn_type indicates)
cust_txn_net AS (
  SELECT
    t.customer_id,
    date(t.txn_date) AS txn_date,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN lower(t.txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit','cr','in','buy') THEN t.txn_amount
          WHEN lower(t.txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw','debit','dr','out','sell') THEN -t.txn_amount
          ELSE t.txn_amount
        END) AS net_change
  FROM txns t
  GROUP BY t.customer_id, date(t.txn_date)
),
-- generate calendar days for each customer within their range
cust_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    cr.customer_id,
    date(cr.start_date, '+' || (n.n) || ' days') AS day
  FROM cust_range cr,
       (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
        UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
        UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
        UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
        UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
       ) n
  WHERE date(cr.start_date, '+' || (n.n) || ' days') <= cr.end_date
),
-- attach net change per day (0 if no txn)
cust_day_change AS (
  SELECT
    cc.customer_id,
    cc.day AS day,
    IFNULL(ctn.net_change, 0) AS net_change
  FROM cust_calendar cc
  LEFT JOIN cust_txn_net ctn
    ON cc.customer_id = ctn.customer_id AND cc.day = ctn.txn_date
),
-- compute running balance per customer per day: cumulative sum of net_change ordered by day.
-- SQLite doesn't have built-in window framing with partition order in older versions; use correlated subquery
cust_day_balance AS (
  SELECT
    cdc.customer_id,
    cdc.day,
    -- cumulative sum up to and including this day
    (SELECT SUM(net_change)
     FROM cust_day_change cdc2
     WHERE cdc2.customer_id = cdc.customer_id
       AND date(cdc2.day) <= date(cdc.day)
    ) AS raw_balance
  FROM cust_day_change cdc
),
-- replace negative balances with zero
cust_day_balance_nonneg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    day,
    CASE WHEN raw_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE raw_balance END AS balance
  FROM cust_day_balance
),
-- month key
cust_day_month AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    day,
    substr(day,1,7) AS month -- YYYY-MM
  FROM cust_day_balance_nonneg
),
-- per customer-month maximum daily balance
cust_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    cdm.customer_id,
    cdm.month,
    MAX(cdbn.balance) AS max_daily_balance
  FROM cust_day_month cdm
  JOIN cust_day_balance_nonneg cdbn
    ON cdm.customer_id = cdbn.customer_id AND cdm.day = cdbn.day
  GROUP BY cdm.customer_id, cdm.month
)
-- final: sum per month across customers, ordered ascending
SELECT
  month AS month,
  SUM(max_daily_balance) AS monthly_total_max_daily_balance
FROM cust_month_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rewrite:
Task: Compute, for each product, the number of times it was viewed, the number of times it was added to the shopping cart, the number of times it was left in the cart without being purchased, and the number of actual purchases, excluding any events where the product's page id is in (1, 2, 12, 13).
Required outputs: product identifier (product id or equivalent); view_count: integer count of times the product was viewed; add_to_cart_count: integer count of times the product was added to the shopping cart; left_in_cart_count: integer count of times the product was left in the cart without being purchased; purchase_count: integer count of actual purchases of the product
Filters: Exclude any rows/events where product's page id IN (1, 2, 12, 13); Only include products that appear in the dataset after applying the page id filter

subgoals.text: Filter the raw event log to exclude any events whose product page id is in the excluded set (1,2,12,13). Keep only events that relate to a product (views, add-to-cart, purchases, cart removals/abandonment events).

Normalize and classify each filtered event into canonical boolean flags for the product-level actions of interest (is_view, is_add_to_cart, is_purchase, is_cart_removal_or_abandon). Keep one row per event with these flags and canonical product identifier and timestamp.

Aggregate the normalized event flags to compute counts per product: number of views, number of add-to-cart events, number of cart-left-without-purchase events, and number of purchases. Only include products that appear after the page_id filter (i.e., present in product_event_flags).

final_sql:
WITH events_filtered AS (
SELECT
  -- event_id: construct stable id from visit_id + sequence_number (keeps PK-ish from source)
  visit_id || ':' || CAST(sequence_number AS TEXT) AS event_id,
  event_type,
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id AS product_id,
  cookie_id AS user_id,
  event_time AS timestamp,
  shopping_cart_events.page_id AS page_id,
  visit_id AS session_id,
  NULL AS quantity,
  NULL AS other_event_metadata
FROM shopping_cart_events
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
  ON shopping_cart_events.page_id = shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_id
WHERE
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id IS NOT NULL
  AND shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
),
product_event_flags AS (
SELECT
  ef.event_id AS event_id,
  ef.product_id AS product_id,
  ef.user_id AS user_id,
  ef.timestamp AS timestamp,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_view,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_add_to_cart,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type IN (3,4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_cart_removal_or_abandon,
  CASE WHEN ef.event_type = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_purchase
FROM events_filtered ef
),
product_action_counts AS (
SELECT
  product_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_view = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS view_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_add_to_cart = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_cart_removal_or_abandon = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS left_in_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_purchase = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchase_count
FROM product_event_flags
GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT
  product_id,
  view_count,
  add_to_cart_count,
  left_in_cart_count,
  purchase_count
FROM product_action_counts
ORDER BY product_id

question: Analyze the annual average purchase price per Bitcoin by region, computed as the total dollar amount spent divided by the total quantity purchased each year, excluding the first year's data for each region. Then, for each year, rank the regions based on these average purchase prices, and calculate the annual percentage change in cost for each region compared to the previous year.
rewrite:
Task: For each region and calendar year (excluding each region's first year of purchase data), compute the annual average purchase price per Bitcoin as (total dollar amount spent in that region and year) divided by (total quantity of Bitcoin purchased in that region and year); then, for each year, rank the regions by that average purchase price and also compute, for each region and year, the percentage change in that average price relative to the immediately preceding year for the same region.
Required outputs: year (calendar year); region; total_dollars_spent (sum of dollars spent in that region and year); total_quantity_purchased (sum of quantity purchased in that region and year); average_price_per_bitcoin (total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased); region_rank_within_year (rank of region for that year ordered by average_price_per_bitcoin descending or specify ordering); pct_change_from_previous_year (percentage change in average_price_per_bitcoin compared to the previous calendar year for the same region; NULL if previous-year data absent)
Filters: Exclude rows where the year is the first calendar year that has any purchase records for that region (i.e., omit each region's earliest year present in the data).; Exclude any year/region combinations where total_quantity_purchased is zero or NULL to avoid division by zero.; Use calendar year derived from the purchase timestamp/date fields; treat year as integer (e.g., 2021).
Sort/limit: Order the final result first by year ascending, then by region_rank_within_year ascending; no row limit.

subgoals.text: Select raw purchase records with purchase timestamp cast to calendar year and canonical region and numeric dollar and quantity fields; exclude records with NULL region or NULL/zero quantity or NULL dollars at this stage only if schema forces. This is the base cohort of purchases with a year column.

Aggregate the raw purchases to one row per region and calendar year computing total dollars spent and total quantity purchased. Also compute the region's first_purchase_year (earliest year with any purchases) so later filtering can drop each region's first year.

subgoals.text: From annual_region_totals compute average_price_per_bitcoin (total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased), exclude rows where purchase_year equals first_purchase_year for that region and where total_quantity_purchased is zero/NULL, then within each calendar year rank regions by average_price_per_bitcoin (descending for highest price = rank 1) and compute percentage change of average_price_per_bitcoin versus the prior calendar year for the same region using a lag; produce final columns required by the question.

final_sql:
WITH raw_purchases_year_region AS (
SELECT
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_id AS purchase_id,
  COALESCE(bitcoin_members.region, bitcoin_transactions.ticker, NULL) AS region,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', substr(bitcoin_transactions.txn_date, -4) || '-' || 
       printf('%02d', CASE 
         WHEN instr(bitcoin_transactions.txn_date, '-') = 3 THEN substr(bitcoin_transactions.txn_date, 1, 2)
         ELSE NULL END) || '-01') AS INTEGER) AS purchase_year,
  (bitcoin_transactions.quantity * 1.0) * (1.0) AS dollars_spent,
  bitcoin_transactions.quantity AS quantity_purchased,
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_time AS purchase_timestamp
FROM bitcoin_transactions
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members ON bitcoin_transactions.member_id = bitcoin_members.member_id
WHERE bitcoin_transactions.quantity IS NOT NULL
  AND bitcoin_transactions.quantity != 0
  AND bitcoin_transactions.txn_id IS NOT NULL
  AND (bitcoin_members.region IS NOT NULL OR bitcoin_transactions.ticker IS NOT NULL)
),
annual_region_totals AS (
SELECT
  region,
  purchase_year,
  SUM(dollars_spent) AS total_dollars_spent,
  SUM(quantity_purchased) AS total_quantity_purchased,
  MIN(purchase_year) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS first_purchase_year
FROM raw_purchases_year_region
GROUP BY region, purchase_year
)
SELECT
  purchase_year AS year,
  region,
  total_dollars_spent,
  total_quantity_purchased,
  total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased AS average_price_per_bitcoin,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY purchase_year ORDER BY (total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) DESC) AS region_rank_within_year,
  CASE
    WHEN LAG(total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY purchase_year) IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE ((total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) - LAG(total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY purchase_year))
         / LAG(total_dollars_spent / total_quantity_purchased) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY purchase_year)
  END AS pct_change_from_previous_year
FROM annual_region_totals
WHERE purchase_year IS NOT NULL
  AND total_quantity_purchased IS NOT NULL
  AND total_quantity_purchased <> 0
  AND purchase_year <> first_purchase_year
ORDER BY year ASC, region_rank_within_year ASC

question: Using the "bitcoin_prices" table, please calculate the daily percentage change in trading volume for each ticker from August 1 to August 10, 2021, ensuring that any volume ending in "K" or "M" is accurately converted to thousands or millions, any "-" volume is treated as zero, only non-zero volumes are used to determine the previous day's volume, and the results are ordered by ticker and date.
rewrite:
Task: For each ticker in the bitcoin_prices table, compute the daily percentage change in trading volume for each date from 2021-08-01 through 2021-08-10 inclusive, converting volume strings that end with 'K' or 'M' into numeric values (thousands or millions), treating any '-' volume as zero, and when computing the percentage change for a given date use the most recent prior date with a non-zero converted volume for the same ticker as the 'previous day's' volume.

subgoals.text: Select rows from the bitcoin_prices source restricted to the target date range (2021-08-01 through 2021-08-10) and preserve one row per ticker+date as present in the table.

WITH prices_date_filter AS (
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS date,
  volume AS raw_volume
FROM bitcoin_prices
WHERE market_date >= '2021-08-01' AND market_date <= '2021-08-10'
),
volume_normalized AS (
SELECT
  p.ticker AS ticker,
  p.date AS date,
  CASE
    WHEN p.raw_volume = '-' THEN 0.0
    WHEN substr(p.raw_volume, -1, 1) = 'K' THEN CAST(replace(substr(p.raw_volume, 1, length(p.raw_volume)-1), ',', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
    WHEN substr(p.raw_volume, -1, 1) = 'M' THEN CAST(replace(substr(p.raw_volume, 1, length(p.raw_volume)-1), ',', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
    ELSE CAST(replace(p.raw_volume, ',', '') AS REAL)
  END AS volume
FROM prices_date_filter p
),
prev_non_zero_and_pct_change AS (
SELECT
  v.ticker AS ticker,

WITH

params AS (

    date('2020-06-15') AS after_start,
    date('2020-06-15','+12 weeks','-1 day') AS after_end
),

  SELECT
    cw.*,

  FROM sales s
  JOIN params p
    ON (date(s.wd_iso) BETWEEN p.before_start AND p.before_end)
     OR (date(s.wd_iso) BETWEEN p.after_start AND p.after_end)
),
-- helper to sum sales by attribute and period

  SELECT
    'region' AS attribute_type,
    region AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY region

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'platform' AS attribute_type,
    platform AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY platform

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'age band' AS attribute_type,
    age_band AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY age_band

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'demographic' AS attribute_type,
    demographic AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY demographic

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'customer type' AS attribute_type,
    customer_type AS attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT before_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN date(wd_iso) BETWEEN (SELECT after_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params) THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after

-- compute percentage change per attribute value, excluding zero sales_before
